cross_module_seam_definitions.description: The Runtime-owned authoring API reads only the caller-supplied project root and exact Skill/Module closure, then returns path-free content; Registry registration and production execution never read the authoring tree.
Only Runtime compilation defines Runtime release canonicalization and hashing.
Every Registry-release binding enters a candidate as ref plus release_sha256 and is verified at registration, except the declared Schema Asset ref plus schema_sha256 content binding.
Execution Profile compilation and selection remain independent from semantic Module compilation and contain no Context or retry semantic binding.
Runtime owns closed Behavior, Evaluation, Retry, and Execution Variant Policy schemas and validates every new Policy before registration.
Runtime compiles Workflow releases from content-only candidates; Module refs bind release hashes and other Workflow refs bind exact supplied content hashes.
Retry Policy is the max_attempts authority; Execution resolves it and Ledger accepts only matching primitive ref hash and value inputs.

Only Registry validates and registers release closure and owns Module/Workflow active pointers; the Runtime-owned persistence writer writes Runtime logical tables through a deployment-supplied connection factory and fixed namespace, while the deployment host owns physical PostgreSQL infrastructure.
Skill review metadata is not a Runtime release family or normal Module execution dependency.
Adapter release admission remains outside Slice 2; Slice 2 preserves existing Execution Profile adapter identity without inventing an Adapter family.
Provider-neutral strict_output_schema_projection is owned by Foundation and consumed by Registry compilation and Invocation with byte-identical evidence.
Module-local, Registry, PostgreSQL, Runtime policy execution, and real-host tests remain ordered owner-specific gates; a higher-layer failure cannot widen a lower Slice.

migration_and_compatibility: Add content-only Agent and non-Agent Runtime candidate compilation and prove one fixed JSON candidate's Module Prompt, Policy, input, and output contracts before Registry PostgreSQL work; then install the side-by-side PostgreSQL v2 target.
The migration-control table plus database triggers fence v1 writes until cutover or explicit rollback; no intermediate Runtime writer deployment is required.

Runtime-repository build/migration tooling outside the product import graph consumes one hash-pinned path-free host RegistryMigrationCandidateSet, produces the complete RegistrySchemaMigrationPlan, and invokes the code-owned abort command.
Replace ambient authoring discovery with the explicit Runtime-owned Module authoring API and migrate Source-to-Evidence as the first real seam proof.
Migrate remaining domain release assemblers, turn the full real composition gate green, then remove ambient Runtime tree discovery and every Package-era host reference in one coherent cutover.
Move provider-neutral output-schema projection to Foundation and update Invocation plus the real host consumer to that one public surface.

Retire the predecessor Workflow registry and plugin path, split surviving cross-responsibility contracts to their semantic owners without behavior change, and move WorkflowRelease-to-backend graph projection from Registry to Durability.

Retire WorkflowExecutionProfileSelection and WorkflowNodeExecutionProfileBinding; the Execution Variant Policy Release owns profile selection while the pinned origin graph carries per-position Module identity.
Update canonical Runtime Design Docs and regenerate their standalone-package projections in the same slice.
Do not add registry_module_exporting or another compatibility shim.
Rebuild the downstream consumer manifest with owner decisions and turn the real composition and PostgreSQL gates green.

Every v1 release row receives an unchanged, reissued, or retired identity disposition; every legacy v1 admission receives a removal disposition; every Module/Workflow active pointer receives a copy, replacement, or removal disposition; only byte-identical canonical payloads retain identity.
rollback_boundary: The v1 schema remains authoritative but durably write-fenced by PostgreSQL triggers until Software Delivery switches the configured schema to a validated ready v2 target. Before any v2 execution or v2-only selection, an administrator explicitly drops the named unselected v2 target out of band, then abort removes the triggers and fence row, restores the prior Runtime/host commits, and points the host back to v1. After either event, predecessor rollback is forbidden and recovery requires a separately reviewed later Registry migration outside Slice 2; no rollback restores Skill Package authority or Runtime host-tree discovery.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime production contains no authoring-tree read; the explicit authoring API requires a caller-supplied project root and exact identities, performs no ambient or sibling discovery, and returns no path-bearing candidate or release.
Module and Execution Profile compilation are independent, and Execution Profile has no Context or retry semantic binding.
Workflow releases are compiled by Runtime from repository-independent exact content candidates; hosts do not construct hash-bearing Workflow records.
Runtime Module Release contains no Skill or authoring-source provenance.
execution_release_ref remains only as a legacy-named opaque host execution-binding content ref for decode compatibility and is not an eleventh Registry release family.

Ten release families have one canonical payload/hash identity; every Registry dependency ref binds the named release hash except the declared Schema Asset content-hash binding; other Workflow refs bind exact supplied content; policy documents validate against Runtime-owned registered Schema Assets; Adapter admission remains outside Slice 2.

Retry Policy is the sole max_attempts authority; Ledger receives caller-validated primitive ref/hash/value inputs, records only the existing bounded max_attempts projection, and requires no schema migration.

Every new Schema Asset registration fails closed when the schema is invalid or validation support is unavailable; ordinary persisted-catalog reload verifies stored identity and closure without rerunning authoring-time schema validation.
Ordinary PostgreSQL operations verify one committed supported schema release and perform no DDL.

Every v1 release row has an unchanged, reissued, or retired identity disposition; every legacy v1 admission has a removal disposition; every Module/Workflow active pointer has a copy, replacement, or removal disposition; only unchanged canonical payloads retain exact identity.

The reproducible migration-plan tool accepts only a hash-pinned path-free host RegistryMigrationCandidateSet, owns v1 fingerprint/decode/disposition/reissue generation, and abort cannot remove the write fence while a v2 target exists.
trading_platform contains no Package-era Runtime contract and uses the single Runtime-owned Module authoring API.
The predecessor Workflow registry, Registry-to-Durability projection edge, and cross-responsibility Registry contract facade are removed.
Canonical Runtime Design Docs and generated standalone-package projections match the implemented release model.
The T2 Registry candidate uses the same four peer Policy families and hash bindings before registration.

The recorded real composition and real PostgreSQL gates pass; the Lumentum gate performs one live configured Adapter call and commits a schema-valid completed EVALUATION result bound to exact Module, Profile, input, and output hashes.

Representative host testing closes Module-local JSON and I/O gates before in-memory Registry closure, PostgreSQL persistence, and final real-host integration; PostgreSQL is never the setup mechanism for Module semantic or I/O correctness.
No compatibility shim, duplicate release family, or second authoring authority remains.
Independent Opus 5 xhigh engineering review accepts the implementation.
